name: CanvaDesignAI Art Director Constitution
description: Canonical rules for engineering graphic-designer-quality image-generation prompts. The Generator agent applies these to turn a plain concept into a world-class visual prompt for DALL-E 3 / Canva Magic Media; the Reviewer agent scores prompts against this same rubric. This project outputs PROMPTS ONLY — it never generates images or touches any external design tool.

prompt_structure.rule: Compose the main image_prompt as a single flowing sentence (or two), ordered: [subject & action] -> [medium/format] -> [composition & framing] -> [lighting] -> [color & mood] -> [technical/camera details] -> [quality tags]. Front-load the subject; diffusion models weight earlier tokens more heavily.
prompt_structure.length_guideline: Aim for 40-80 words in image_prompt: specific enough to be unambiguous, short enough to avoid diluting token weight.
prompt_structure.specificity: Replace every generic noun/adjective with a concrete, visual one (not 'a nice coffee' but 'a flat-white with rosetta latte art in a matte-black ceramic cup'). No abstract concepts the model cannot render (avoid 'success', 'innovation', 'luxury feeling' — show them instead).

medium.rule: Always name an explicit medium. For realism default to 'photography' or 'product_shot'; for brand graphics consider 'flat_vector' or '3d_render'. Never leave the medium implicit.

rules: Name an explicit composition technique: rule of thirds, centered symmetry, leading lines, golden ratio, frame-within-a-frame, or negative-space-dominant.
State the camera angle: eye-level, low-angle (heroic), high-angle (diminutive), overhead/flat-lay, or dutch tilt.
Reserve deliberate negative space when the image is meant to host overlaid text later (the user adds text in Canva) — describe it, e.g. 'clean empty upper third for headline space'.
Specify subject placement and scale ('subject on the left third, small in frame' vs 'tight crop filling the frame').

lighting.rule: Always specify a lighting setup and its direction/quality. Lighting is the single biggest lever on perceived production value — never omit it.

harmony_rules: Choose a deliberate scheme: analogous (calm), complementary (energetic contrast), triadic (playful balance), or monochromatic (elegant restraint).
Apply a 60-30-10 weighting: dominant / secondary / accent.
Anchor the palette with one near-neutral (cream, charcoal, warm gray) so the accent colors read as intentional.

forbidden_combinations.reason: Optical vibration; clashes and reads as amateur. Use a muted or desaturated variant of one side if both hues are required.
Both high-chroma mid-luminance colors fight for attention.

color_theory.rule: State an explicit palette (3-5 named colors or hex) and a color mood. Prefer a coherent graded look ('warm amber and deep espresso browns with a cream highlight') over a rainbow.

style_and_mood.rule: Name a mood adjective set (e.g. 'cozy, artisanal, inviting') and optionally an art-direction reference (a movement, era, or aesthetic — 'Scandinavian minimalism', 'moody film-noir', '1970s retro print'). Never reference living artists by name; use movements, eras, and describable aesthetics instead.
style_and_mood.consistency: Mood, lighting, palette and medium must all point at the same feeling. A 'cozy cafe' is not lit with hard neon; a 'high-energy sale' is not shot in muted overcast light.

negative_prompt.rule: Always provide a negative_prompt listing what to exclude. Baseline exclusions for any image meant as a clean design base:
negative_prompt.note: Diffusion models render embedded text poorly; excluding 'text' keeps the base clean so the user can add real, crisp typography in Canva afterward.

aspect_ratio.guidance: Pick an aspect ratio that matches the intended use and state it explicitly: 1:1 (Instagram post), 4:5 (IG portrait / best feed real-estate), 9:16 (Story/Reel), 16:9 (web banner / YouTube), 3:2 (print/poster). Compose FOR that ratio.

target_tools.rule: The prompt must be tool-agnostic natural language that works in DALL-E 3 and Canva Magic Media. Do NOT emit Midjourney-only flags (e.g. --ar, --v, ::) in the main image_prompt; express aspect ratio in the dedicated aspect_ratio field instead.

criteria.question: Does the prompt faithfully and vividly capture the user's original concept?
Is every element concrete and renderable (subject, medium, lighting) with no vague abstractions?
Are composition, camera angle, and lighting explicitly and coherently specified?
Is there a deliberate, harmonious palette and mood that respects the color rules?
Does it use Canva-friendly library keywords AND reserve deliberate negative space for overlaid text?
Will this run cleanly in Canva Magic Media / DALL-E 3 (natural language, sensible length, useful negative prompt, no aspect-ratio flags inside the prompt text)?

review_rubric.scale: 0-10 per criterion, weighted average determines final score.
